completedWork: SCANS. test/scan/sql.test.js (T20, 4 tests): every .prepare( and .exec( call under src/ and scripts/ is static SQL or an allow-listed constant. DEVIATION FROM THE SPEC, stated openly: the spec asks to forbid template literals in db.prepare( calls; the code base builds about thirty statements from constants and ? placeholder lists with template literals, so a literal ban fails correct code. The test pins what the ban protects: a per-file allow-list (each entry with its reason, a stale-entry check, the routes and http layer scanned with an empty list), so any new interpolation fails. test/scan/live-refusal.test.js (NFR3/FU-37, 15 tests): the live model script, each test/live/paypal/*.test.js, the launcher, evaluateLaunch and evaluateLiveLaunch, and the package scripts exit 2 without their flag and print the fixed message only. test/scan/secrets.test.js (RS-29): appended section scanning public/, fixtures, recorded live responses, the PNG text chunks of every screenshot under test/browser/out (skipped, with a reason, when there is none), README and docs, and config redaction errors with canaries and secret shapes. LABELLING. test/api/labelling.test.js (RS-34 [D], 13 tests) for the fake adapter and the Sandbox adapter against the loopback stub: the exact label set of GET /api/config, provider, simulated and sandbox on every payment object, demo and price notice, config refusals. test/browser/labelling.test.js (RS-34 [B], 4 tests): banners on every route, payment badges, demo data, the price notice, the provider's own approval page and the admin provider list for both adapters at 360 and 1280 px (the sandbox environment sets RS_TEST_HOOKS undefined because the Sandbox adapter refuses it). test/browser/six-questions.test.js (RS-35, 2 tests): the six answers in order with provenance, decision trace, rejection codes with explanations, cents totals, commitment next to offer, compensation state. test/browser/a11y-states.test.js (NFR2, 8 tests): the keyboard-only purchase (register to complete, no pointer), empty, loading, error with Retry, timeout, degraded extraction, expired reservation with Re-plan, refunding and failed-needs-attention (Contact the organiser) at 360 px (FU-51), the admin forced-reset stranded list audited and walkable, the forced-reset text per adapter in Chromium, and the RLM and zero-width refusal reason isolated in <bdi> (the two g1 items that were unverified). Helpers: a11y-audit.js (hand-written audit: names, 44 px targets, computed 4.5:1 contrast, focus indicators through real Tab, no horizontal scroll), keyboard.js, api-purchase.js, and approval-roundtrip.js gained stub and keyboard options. EVIDENCE TABLE. docs/evidence-table.md: 45 rows, 28 verified, 2 fake-only (RS-25, RS-34), 15 LIVE-DEPENDENT (RS-01, 02, 03, 05, 18 to 24, 26, 31, 32, NFR6), each with suites, tests by file and title, the ev ids of runs on the final tree, and the unverified part with its blocker (LIVE-M1, LIVE-P1, LIVE-P2, OQ-D5, USER-Q9; A2 and SEC-18 where they apply); the FU-52 list that no live file covers, identical to the runbook (FU-44: cross-merchant signature rejection is in it, as a documentation branch); the mutation proofs; the date-robustness command; the limits. test/scan/evidence-table.test.js (11 tests) checks all 45 ids once, the status vocabulary, that every named test is in its file, that every non-verified or live-tagged row names a blocker, the SEC-18, A2, F-TR-18, F-TR-9 and Q9 wordings, parity with the runbook list, and, when the project record is present, that each cited run exited 0 and shows each named test as ok and not skipped (reported as skipped in a clean checkout). DATE ROBUSTNESS. test/helpers/shift-clock.mjs committed with its blind spots in the header; one full locked +30-day npm test passed (ev:ev-mv4dxpjf-01ff87f2) and a separate run proves the preload is active under that command (Date.now() 30.000 days ahead in the process and in a child, file times shifted, explicit utimes round trip: ev:ev-mv4dy7qb-017f57f9). RS-36 (I): a new inspection of the final domain/derive.js against the final derivation table (F-TR-9) is NOT part of this evidence; the phase B review did it for revision 2 and the rows added later are pinned only by tests.
Browser evidence is Chromium only, Linux only, Node 22.22 only; other browsers, screen readers and real touch devices were not run.

T20 is a deviation: an allow-list of interpolations instead of the literal ban on template literals in prepare( calls (about thirty correct call sites would fail the literal ban). The reviewer should accept or reject the deviation.

Focus on a native date-time control is shown by comparing pictures of the focused and unfocused control (visible inputs only), because the control has no app focus ring and no :focus-visible style on its host; this is a weaker check than a style assertion and cannot show which part of the control is highlighted.
RS-29 matches secret SHAPES by patterns plus canary values; a secret of an unknown shape would pass the pattern part. Screenshots are scanned for file names and PNG text chunks, not pixels.

The table cites runs made before the table's last edit (its ids and three prose sections were written after them); the verification run is on the final bytes. The cited-run check of the table test is skipped in a clean checkout (10 skipped there, with printed reasons), so it is not part of the clean-checkout pass count.

The clock-shift tool does not move Chromium, SQLite, FileHandle.stat, string times to utimes, Intl.DateTimeFormat without a date, or children spawned with a minimal environment (listed in its header); a passing +30-day run says nothing about them.
The lockfile lacks node_modules/fsevents (macOS only, optional). The regenerated lock is at scratchpad/g3-lock/package-lock.json (sha256 d870b67d...dd62); applying it is for the lock's owner.
Statements about the hackathon rules and the PayPal dashboard in docs/submission and docs/runbooks remain unverified against primary sources (g2 handoff).
